uncited: It solves the problem of reconstructing and rendering dynamic 3D content from multi-view video by extending static 3D Gaussian Splatting with temporal tracking and deformation constraints.

It differs from its parent [Dynamic 3D Gaussian Splatting](5703-dynamic-3d-gaussian-splatting.md) by explicitly defining the tracking mechanism (linking Gaussians to 3D point motion) and from [GaussianFlow](6149-gaussianflow.md) by its reliance on persistent synthesis rather than flow-based deformation fields.

The method maintains a set of 3D Gaussian primitives $\mathcal{G} = \{g_i\}$, where each primitive $g_i$ is defined at time $t$ by its position $\boldsymbol{\mu}_i^t$, orientation $q_i^t$, scale $s_i^t$, opacity $\alpha_i^t$, and spherical harmonic coefficients $c_i^t$.
The core innovation is the temporal update of $\boldsymbol{\mu}_i^t$ and $q_i^t$ via tracking.

- **Gaussian Primitive:** A struct containing $\boldsymbol{\mu} \in \mathbb{R}^3$, $q \in \mathbb{R}^4$ (normalized quaternion), $s \in \mathbb{R}^3$, $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$, $c \in \mathbb{R}^K$ (SH coefficients).
**Keyframe Management:** Maintain primitives only from a set of past keyframes.
- Tracking Model: Pre-trained 2D point tracking model.
It sets itself apart by explicitly using a pre-trained 2D point tracker and EDG for motion propagation, rather than learning deformation fields directly.
- **Time Complexity:** Depends on the 2D tracking model and the number of Gaussians.
Triangulation is $O(N)$ per Gaussian per frame.
- **Memory Complexity:** Proportional to the number of Gaussians and keyframes.
Dynamic 3D Gaussians was introduced as part of the broader 3D Gaussian Splatting family to handle dynamic scenes.
It builds on [3D Gaussian Splatting](52-3d-gaussian-splatting.md) and [Dynamic 3D Gaussian Splatting](5703-dynamic-3d-gaussian-splatting.md).
